Subject: Next steps: Redwood procurement & approvals for Acme POC

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the POC and clarify the procurement path:

Recap (from my notes):
- Scope: 3-week POC, up to 50k tokens/day, Redwood-hosted Dedicated or Private depending on security needs.
- Success criteria: latency under 300ms p50, integration with product search, two eval prompt sets validated.
- Technical contacts: David (VP Product) / engineering team to run integration.

Procurement & commercial questions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Preferred payment method: PO vs corporate card? (Olivia, you mentioned procurement usually issues POs for POCs > $X)
2) Marketplace interest: would Acme prefer to transact via AWS Marketplace or direct Redwood invoice?
3) Budget owner / signatory path: who signs POs for POCs (economic buyer vs CFO)? You noted David Lee as product budget owner — can you confirm the finance sponsor and final signatory?

Attachments: I’m sharing a short procurement checklist that outlines common docs procurement asks for (insurance, SOC2, SOW, order form). I’ve also attached a draft SOW we use for POCs if helpful.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- You: confirm PO vs card and signatory path + loop in procurement contact (if different from procurement@acme.com) — by EOD Thu
- Redwood: send commercial terms and SOW draft for review — by EOD Wed
- Schedule kickoff once PO/approval path is clear

If easier, happy to jump on a quick 20-min call with procurement and your finance sponsor to walk through standard flow.

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Subject: Re: Next steps: Redwood procurement & approvals for Acme POC

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the checklist, super helpful. A few answers from procurement side: 

- Payment method: Acme typically issues a PO for engagements like this. Corporate card is used only for SaaS subscriptions under $5k/yr — so for a 3-week POC we’d expect a PO.
- Marketplace: Procurement prefers Marketplace purchases when possible, but for POCs they will accept direct invoices (fewer catalog requirements). If Redwood can list on AWS Marketplace later that would be ideal, but not required for the POC.
- Budget & signatory path: David Lee is the budget owner for product initiatives; Karen Park (Finance Business Partner) is the finance sponsor who will review terms. Final signatory for POCs < $100k is typically our VP Product (David) but Procurement needs to review CLA/order form.

I’m looping in procurement@acme.com here (they’ll confirm required docs). Attached is our internal PO process doc that shows the steps procurement will follow.

Olivia

--
Olivia Chen

olivia.chen@acme.com

1) We'll prepare a Quote + Order Form that supports PO payment and is compatible with direct invoice or AWS Marketplace later.
2) Signatory question: can you confirm if VP Product (David) signs POs for POCs under $100k, or does Procurement require CFO-level signoff? We’d like to know whether to expect a 1- or 2-signature path for timelines.
3) Can procurement@acme.com confirm required insurance limits and whether a vendor security questionnaire is necessary (we can provide SOC2 report and AICPA artefacts).

I’ll attach our standard SOW + commercial terms preview so your finance/procurement team can review before we send an official quote. If it helps, I’m available to join a short call with procurement + finance sponsor to walk the docs.

- Redwood: send Redwood_Commercial_Terms-v1.pdf + Redwood_SOW_template.pdf (attached) — today

Thanks — looking forward.

Subject: Internal: Acme procurement / discount ask (summary + ask)

Internal summary and ask — Acme (David Lee / Olivia Chen): POC scoped as 3-week Redwood-hosted POC, expected to be invoiced via PO. Budget owner: David Lee (VP Product). Finance sponsor: Karen Park. Procurement prefers PO (Marketplace optional later).

Commercial signal: Product team is motivated; likely to convert if latency & integration checks pass. Ballpark POC ARR-equivalent (list price): ~$25k for the 3-week engagement + support.

Ask:
- Aditya: do I have authority to approve a one-time POC discount up to 15% for this deal? If not, what approval threshold should I route to you/RevOps?
- Neha: any concessions on payment terms we should avoid (we prefer net 30; Acme may request net 45 or 60). Also need guidance on standard PO clauses that procurement tends to redline — ccBreach/liability/indemnity areas to watch?

Next steps I’ll take: will send official quote + SOW to procurement once I get confirmation on signatory path and insurance requirements. Planning to request kickoff dates for next week.

Thanks — LMK if you want a quick sync.
